title: OpenEXR: ID manifest shift exponent overflow
ai_system: Revelio using Claude Haiku 4.5 and Claude Sonnet 4.6
organization: UC Berkeley Revelio research team and affected project maintainers
summary: The Revelio paper identifies a integer overflow / undefined behavior in OpenEXR v3.4.10: id manifest shift exponent overflow. It lists the author-assessed severity as Critical and says the finding was manually validated with a reproducible sanitizer-backed proof of vulnerability through a reachable project test harness. This is Table V item 2 of the seven-project real-world hunt.
ai_role: The paper describes Revelio as using Claude Haiku 4.5 for hypothesis generation and Claude Sonnet 4.6 for proof-of-vulnerability confirmation; its experimental-method section says this configuration was used for the seven-project OSS-Fuzz hunt. The authors state all 19 tabled findings were manually validated and sanitizer-confirmed. The paper does not provide a per-item model trajectory, so the exact division of Claude work within this row is not independently stated.
classification_note: The paper publicly identifies this distinct finding on 2026-06-20. The authors describe the hunt as searching for previously unknown flaws, but this record does not assert exploitation in the wild or operational zero-day status.
remediation_note: The OpenEXR advisory identifies the unbounded shift in readVariableLengthInteger and lists patched releases 3.2.9, 3.3.11, and 3.4.11.

impacts.conditions: When parsing untrusted EXR input with enough variable-length-integer continuation bytes, readVariableLengthInteger() shifts a 64-bit value by 70, which the advisory identifies as undefined behavior. The recorded consequence is this arithmetic/memory-safety defect only; further downstream effects are not established.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited advisory.
